extracted.intended_audience: members of the public (individuals and small businesses) who wish to petition the CFPB, plus stakeholders such as former government employees and paid influencers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance announcing a new CFPB process allowing members of the public to submit petitions for rulemaking, describing scope (new/amend/repeal), public posting for comment, and transparency/ethics-related rules for paid influencers and former government employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct petitions for rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Starting today, members of the public can submit petitions for rulemaking directly to the CFPB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This new program enables individuals to request agency action without intermediaries; the announcement links to a separate page with details on how and where to submit petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public posting to dockets for review and comment
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitions will be posted on public dockets for review and comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions submitted via this process will be made publicly available so others can review and provide comments, enabling public participation in consideration of the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of petitions (new/amend/repeal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of the public can request that the agency pursue a new rule, amend an existing one, or repeal a rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions are not limited to new rules; they may ask the CFPB to change or eliminate existing regulations. For issues that are consumer complaints about specific products/services, use the complaint website instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure requirement for paid influencers and former government employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Former government employees and other individuals who are paid to influence the agency’s rulemaking agenda behind the scenes will be asked to submit their petition for public inspection instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paid influencers and former officials must make their submissions available for public inspection to promote transparency and reduce behind-the-scenes influence (the announcement frames this as part of ethics/revolving-door reforms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and broadened access principle
rubrics_metrics.description: “Americans should be able to easily exercise their Constitutional rights without hiring a high-priced lawyer or lobbyist.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program is explicitly intended to lower barriers so individuals and small businesses can meaningfully petition the agency without needing paid representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with Administrative Conference recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: The new process is in line with recommendations issued by the Administrative Conference of the United States for improving transparency and ensuring that the public has a meaningful opportunity to petition the government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB frames the change as implementing best-practice recommendations for transparency and meaningful public participation; see ACUS guidance for more detailed standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate channel for consumer complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: Consumer complaints about specific financial products or services should be submitted through the CFPB’s complaint website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes rulemaking petitions (policy/regulatory requests) from individual consumer complaints (submitted via the complaint portal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and ethics commitment (addressing 'revolving door')
rubrics_metrics.description: The reforms are part of steps the CFPB is taking to ensure high standards of transparency and ethics, particularly when it comes to addressing the corrosive effects of the 'revolving door.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The announcement references additional staff guidance to report former government employees who may be misusing information obtained while in government; transparency and ethics considerations are central to the petitioning process reforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions as a tool to identify issues for agency action
rubrics_metrics.description: The public’s petitions will help the CFPB identify consumer protection issues worthy of reform, rulemaking, or in need of further clarification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB presents petitions as a mechanism for surfacing issues that may lead to rulemaking or clarificatory action; petitions are evaluated as potential inputs to the agency’s agenda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural details located on rulemaking petitions page
rubrics_metrics.description: Read more about the rulemaking petitions process, including how and where to submit petitions and comments on petitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The press release is a high-level announcement; specific procedural requirements, submission instructions, and comment processes are provided on the linked rulemaking petitions page (follow that link for exact submission formatting, timelines, and docket procedures).
